The Last Times of the World in General, and of Judah and the Church in Particular.</title> <div sID="gen14482" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">The four chapters (the twenty-fourth through the twenty-seventh) form one continuous poetical prophecy: descriptive of the dispersion and successive calamities of the Jews (<reference osisRef="Isa.24.1-Isa.24.12">Is 24:1-12</reference>); the preaching of the Gospel by the first Hebrew converts throughout the world (<reference osisRef="Isa.24.13-Isa.24.16">Is 24:13-16</reference>); the judgments on the adversaries of the Church and its final triumph (<reference osisRef="Isa.24.16-Isa.24.23">Is 24:16-23</reference>); thanksgiving for the overthrow of the apostate faction (<reference osisRef="Isa.25.1-Isa.25.12">Is 25:1-12</reference>), and establishment of the righteous in lasting peace (<reference osisRef="Isa.26.1-Isa.26.21">Is 26:1-21</reference>); judgment on leviathan and entire purgation of the Church (<reference osisRef="Isa.27.1-Isa.27.13">Is 27:1-13</reference>). Having treated of the several nations in particular--</hi>Babylon, Philistia, Moab, Syria, Israel, Egypt, Edom, and Tyre (the miniature representative of all, as all kingdoms flocked into it)--he passes to the last times of the world at large and of Judah the representative and future head of the churches.<div eID="gen14482" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14483" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8735"/><hi type="bold">1. the earth--</hi>rather, "the land" of Judah (so in <reference osisRef="Isa.24.3">Is 24:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.5.6">5, 6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Joel.1.2">Joe 1:2</reference>). The desolation under Nebuchadnezzar prefigured that under Titus. <div eID="gen14483" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 24 Is 24:1-23 . The Last Times of the World in General, and of Judah and the Church in Particular. The four chapters (the twenty-fourth through the twenty-seventh) form one continuous poetical prophecy: descriptive of the dispersion and successive calamities of the Jews ( Is 24:1-12 ); the preaching of the Gospel by the first Hebrew converts throughout the world ( Is 24:13-16 ); the judgments on the adversaries of the Church and its final triumph ( Is 24:16-23 ); thanksgiving for the overthrow of the apostate faction ( Is 25:1-12 ), and establishment of the righteous in lasting peace ( Is 26:1-21 ); judgment on leviathan and entire purgation of the Church ( Is 27:1-13 ). Having treated of the several nations in particular-- Babylon, Philistia, Moab, Syria, Israel, Egypt, Edom, and Tyre (the miniature representative of all, as all kingdoms flocked into it)--he passes to the last times of the world at large and of Judah the representative and future head of the churches. 1. the earth-- rather, "the land" of Judah (so in Is 24:3 , 5, 6 ; Joe 1:2 ). The desolation under Nebuchadnezzar prefigured that under Titus.

Lowth reads, in the islands (<reference osisRef="Ezek.26.18">Eze 26:18</reference>). Rather translate for "fires," "in the regions of morning light," that is, the east, in antithesis to the "isles of the sea," that is, the west [Maurer]. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8749"/><div sID="gen14507" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8749"/>16. Songs to God come in together to Palestine from distant lands, as a grand chorus.<div eID="gen14507" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14508" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">glory to the righteous--</hi>the burden of the songs (<reference osisRef="Isa.26.2">Is 26:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.26.7">7</reference>). Amidst exile, the loss of their temple, and all that is dear to man, their confidence in God is unshaken. These songs recall the joy of other times and draw from Jerusalem in her present calamities, the cry, "My leanness." Horsley translates, "glory to the Just One"; then My leanness expresses his sense of man's corruption, which led the Jews, "the treacherous dealers" (<reference osisRef="Jer.5.11">Jr 5:11</reference>), to crucify the Just One; and his deficiency of righteousness which made him need to be clothed with the righteousness of the Just One (<reference osisRef="Ps.106.15">Psa 106:15</reference>).<div eID="gen14508" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14509" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">treacherous dealers--</hi>the foreign nations that oppress Jerusalem, and overcome it by stratagem (so in <reference osisRef="Isa.21.2">Is 21:2</reference>) [Barnes]. <div eID="gen14509" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8750"/><div sID="gen14510" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8750"/>17. This verse explains the wretchedness spoken of in <reference osisRef="Isa.24.16">Is 24:16</reference>. Jeremiah (<reference osisRef="Jer.48.43">Jr 48:43</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.48.44">44</reference>) uses the same words. They are proverbial; <reference osisRef="Isa.24.18">Is 24:18</reference> expressing that the inhabitants were nowhere safe; if they escaped one danger, they fell into another, and worse, on the opposite side (<reference osisRef="Amos.5.19">Am 5:19</reference>). "Fear" is the term applied to the cords with feathers of all colors which, when fluttered in the air, scare beasts into the pitfall, or birds into the snare. Horsley makes the connection. Indignant at the treatment which the Just One received, the prophet threatens the guilty land with instant vengeance. <div eID="gen14510" type="x-p"/>

navigation_sections.title: CHAPTER 24
navigation_sections.content_plain: CHAPTER 24 Is 24:1-23 . The Last Times of the World in General, and of Judah and the Church in Particular. The four chapters (the twenty-fourth through the twenty-seventh) form one continuous poetical prophecy: descriptive of the dispersion and successive calamities of the Jews ( Is 24:1-12 ); the preaching of the Gospel by the first Hebrew converts throughout the world ( Is 24:13-16 ); the judgments on the adversaries of the Church and its final triumph ( Is 24:16-23 ); thanksgiving for the overthrow of the apostate faction ( Is 25:1-12 ), and establishment of the righteous in lasting peace ( Is 26:1-21 ); judgment on leviathan and entire purgation of the Church ( Is 27:1-13 ). Having treated of the several nations in particular-- Babylon, Philistia, Moab, Syria, Israel, Egypt, Edom, and Tyre (the miniature representative of all, as all kingdoms flocked into it)--he passes to the last times of the world at large and of Judah the representative and future head of the churches.
